verdicts.argument: The quotes are real. FY2025 10-K index p.20 (printed 19) says the Biktarvy negotiated price will be 'substantially lower' and 'may also lead to increased rebates we owe Medicaid agencies and reduced ceiling prices charged to 340B covered entities'. But the spillover warning is NOT new. The FY2024 10-K index p.20 (printed 19), in the same IRA bullet, already says negotiation 'could also affect the Medicaid rebate obligations and the ceiling prices charged to covered entities under Section 340B ... if such prices are lower than the Medicaid Best Price'. What changed is the Biktarvy selection (public Jan 2026) and the word 'substantially'. The math also fails. 7,187 = Part D gross spend 2025 ($4,011M) + Medicaid reimbursed 2024 ($3,176M) (medicare_market.csv biktarvy rows). That adds two different years, and both are pre-rebate payer spend (Part D spend includes pharmacy margin), so dividing by Gilead's U.S. NET Biktarvy sales ($11,467M, 10-K FY2025 index p.40) gives 62.7%, which is not a share of anything. Medicaid net is far below reimbursed amount after statutory and CPI rebates. The '$1,147M per 10%' illustration applies a 10% cut to ALL U.S. Biktarvy sales, but the MFP applies only to Medicare, and the filing does not size the Medicaid/340B spillover. The arithmetic checks (1,147/29,443 = 3.9%), but the scenario is unanchored and starts in 2028.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to: the FY2025 10-K now applies the existing IRA spillover warning to a named drug (Biktarvy, 48.7% of revenue) and says the Medicare price will be 'substantially lower' starting 2028. The 340B wording got stronger ('pervasive violations', index p.21). No dollar sizing is supportable from the filing. Do not present 62.7% as a government-channel share.

verdicts.argument: The deletion is real. FY2024 10-K index p.18 has the nucleoside-paradigm sentence, and a full-text search of FY2025 10-K finds no 'paradigm' sentence and only 'nucleoside' in collaboration notes (index pp.74, 76). Two claims are wrong, though. (1) 'Replaced maximize near-term revenue growth with maximize impact of long-acting' is wrong: FY2024 10-K index p.38 already lists '(ii) maximize impact of long-acting HIV therapies'. FY2025 index p.37 drops (i) and promotes long-acting to first place. (2) '$20.8B oral TAF franchise' is wrong: Total HIV $20,752M (FY2025 index p.40) includes Sunlenca and Yeztugo (long-acting lenacapavir, inside Other HIV) and the Symtuza revenue share. The impact math ('10% migrates = $2,075M') is an arbitrary illustration with no period, no rate, and no netting. Migration to Gilead's own long-acting products (Yeztugo, the next capsid regimens) is not a revenue loss. Nothing here moves revenue, operating income or EPS by a number the sources support.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to a disclosure observation: FY2025 removed the risk sentence tying HIV sales to nucleosides staying the preferred regimen, and promoted long-acting from priority (ii) to (i). Present it as qualitative, not as a $2B exposure.

verdicts.argument: The core numbers hold. FY2025 10-K index p.41 shows GTN $19,953M vs $17,776M (+12%) and 41% vs 38% of gross, and the 10-K itself states '250 bps'. Net product sales were 28,915 vs 28,610 (index p.40). Gross 48,868 vs 46,386 = +5.35%. Rate 40.83% vs 38.32%. The derived claims are wrong in three ways. (a) 'Stopped giving the rebate-vs-other split' is overstated. The FY2025 footnote on index p.41 still gives rebates and chargebacks of $17.5B vs $15.5B, so other deductions are about $2.45B vs $2.28B, about 35.8%/5.0% vs 33.4%/4.9% of gross. Only the printed percentages were dropped. (b) '$1,227M of net revenue lost' treats 2025 gross at the 2024 GTN rate as attainable net. Much of the gross growth is list inflation: Biktarvy WAC +5.9% on 2025-01-01 (wac_increases.csv rows 544-546) against gross +5.35%. A list increase that is rebated away raises GTN dollars and the GTN rate without ever having been net revenue. Mix also moves the rate: Veklury, a hospital product, fell $888M, and Descovy rose $645M (index p.40). (c) The '$327M unexplained' compares a company-wide realized residual to a GUIDANCE assumption scoped to HIV. The ~$900M is 'expected headwind ... in 2025' on the JPM 2026 slide p.5 tied to HIV revenue, and 'No change to other assumptions including ~$900M Medicare Part D Redesign impact' on the 2025Q3 slides p.25. On the grade-A 2025Q3 call p.12, the $900M is the analyst's (Mohit Bansal) number, and the CCO (Johanna Mercier) says only that 'those assumptions have not changed'. The 10-K says Part D also hit Liver Disease (index p.41). The residual is therefore not a finding.
verdicts.correction: Keep: the GTN rate rose about 250 bps to 41% while gross grew about 5.3% and net grew 1.1%, and the 10-K attributes it primarily to Part D redesign. Drop the '$1.2B lost' and '$327M unexplained' framing. If a dollar figure is wanted, say that 100 bps of GTN on about $48.9B gross equals about $489M of net sales (1.7% of revenue), as a sensitivity. Replace 'stopped giving the split' with 'stopped printing the percentages; rebates and chargebacks are still given in dollars ($17.5B vs $15.5B)'.

verdicts.argument: Every operand checks against the source. FY2025 10-K index p.80: total inventory 4,368 vs 3,589 (+21.7%), WIP 1,306 vs 847 (+54.2%), other long-term assets 2,594 vs 1,879 (+38.1%), and the $613M pre-commercial Trodelvy statement. Index p.79: AR net 4,913 vs 4,420 (+11.2%). Index p.42: COGS 6,234 vs 6,251. Index p.45: OCF $10,019M vs $10,828M (-7%). Index p.46: management names the inventory build and AR timing as OCF drags. 10-Q 2026Q2 index p.21: $568M, total inventory 4,298, AR 5,055. The long-term increase is 715 of the 779 total increase (92%). Caveats on the math: (1) DIO uses GAAP COGS, which includes acquired-intangible amortization (GAAP product GM 78.4% vs about 86% non-GAAP, slides p.25), so the 210 to 256 day level is understated. The direction holds. (2) The $568M write-down is a one-time, contingent charge, about 4.3% of FY2025 non-GAAP OI (568/13,193 checks, but it mixes a June 2026 balance with FY2025 OI). It is not a recurring OI hit, and Gilead could exclude it from non-GAAP. (3) The ASCENT-07 miss (HR+/HER2- 1L, index p.23) is unrelated to whether FDA approves a manufacturing process. The 10-K says it caused no impairment. (4) The H1 2026 trend is reversing: total inventory and the pre-commercial balance are both down.
verdicts.correction: State it as: a 2025 working-capital build (inventory +$779M, mostly long-term raw materials and WIP; AR +$493M) cut OCF 7%, and it includes $613M (now $568M) of Trodelvy made on a not-yet-approved process. That is a one-time write-down exposure of about 4% of non-GAAP OI. Drop the ASCENT-07 link, and note the partial unwind in H1 2026.

verdicts.argument: Confirmed. FY2025 10-K index p.41: $400M of previously constrained IP-sale revenue, with royalty/contract revenue at $527M vs $144M. Q3 2025 release p.1: 'not expected to reoccur', and it names the $400M as a driver of non-GAAP EPS $2.47. Proxy index p.115 lists it as a comp exclusion. Proxy index p.116: non-GAAP OI $13,193M includes it, and adjusted OI is $12,785M after -400. On EPS, 8.15 - 0.54 + 0.56 - 0.25 = 7.92, so the $0.25 is subtracted even though the table prints it without parentheses. 10-Q 2026Q2 index p.33 (printed 32): $156M more recognized in Q2 2026. Materiality passes: $400M is 1.4% of revenue, 3.0% of non-GAAP OI, and 3.1% of non-GAAP EPS. The $0.25 is consistent with 400 x (1-0.19)/about 1.25B shares. Small issues: the Q2 2026 '~$0.10' scales by the 2025 per-share rate, although Q2 2026 is a non-GAAP loss quarter with a different tax and share base, so treat it as approximate. 'Near-100% margin' is consistent with the proxy removing $400M of OI for $400M of revenue. The 'IP sale' is a constrained-consideration true-up, so further recognitions are possible, which is the point.
verdicts.correction: Keep. Phrase the 2026 piece as 'about $0.10 (approximate)' and note that the Q3 2025 release named the item as a non-GAAP EPS driver, so it was disclosed, but it was not removed from non-GAAP.

verdicts.argument: The quotes are on the cited pages. Grade-A 2025Q3 call p.12: Johanna Mercier, 'real demand-driven growth'. 10-Q 2026Q2 index p.32: the three-month sentence 'higher average realized price, favorable inventory dynamics and higher demand'. Slides 2026Q2 p.9. The U.S. Biktarvy arithmetic checks: 2,981 vs 2,799 = +$182M (+6.5%), 10-Q index p.11. The contradiction mixes two years, though. The October 2025 remark is about 2025 growth, and the FY2025 10-K (index p.40) confirms 2025 Biktarvy growth was demand-driven with realized price DOWN (Part D). A 2026 price recovery against a Part D-depressed 2025 base does not contradict it. The candidate also cherry-picks the quarter. The six-month sentence on the next page (10-Q index p.33) reads 'higher demand ... and average realized price', with demand first and no inventory. Driver order in MD&A prose is not a magnitude ranking. The 'half of growth is price/inventory' is an assumption with no source. It equals about $91M a quarter, or about 1.2% of revenue annualized, and the inventory part is a timing shift, not lost revenue.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to: in Q2 2026, Gilead attributes Biktarvy's YoY growth partly to realized price from channel mix and an inventory build, and the slide notes lower QoQ demand. The components are unquantified. Do not call it a reversal of the 2025 'demand-driven' statement.

verdicts.argument: The label facts check. Yeztugo continuation is 927 mg every 6 months (label section 2.3, p.5). Apretude is 600 mg every 2 months (section 2.5, p.7). The ASP rows also check: J0738 16.133 (2025Q4) to 16.016 (2026Q4) = -0.7%; J0739 7.020 to 7.278 = +3.7%. Maintenance-year cost $29,694 vs $26,201. The impact fails materiality and attribution. The '$35M a year' applies the 4.4-point RELATIVE gap change, most of which is ViiV raising Apretude, to Gilead's revenue. Gilead's own price drift of -0.7% on an $800M guide (2025Q4 slides p.12) is about $6M, or 0.02% of revenue. Even $35M is 0.12% of revenue, far below the 1% threshold. A newly launched drug's first payment limits are also set from WAC before ASP data exist, so early drift reflects method more than discounting, and the series is Medicare Part B only, while the candidate itself says the payer mix is mostly commercial. The estimate also cites a '$1B 2026 target' while the cited guide is ~$800M.
verdicts.correction: As fine print, keep only the label asymmetry (dosing frequency, no hypersensitivity/hepatotoxicity/depression W&P, inducer handling). Drop the 'discounting the label advantage away' claim and the $35M figure, which is immaterial and misattributed.

verdicts.argument: The label difference is real. Biktarvy label v22 p.1 indicates treatment-experienced patients who are not suppressed and have no resistance substitutions, while Dovato section 1 (p.2) and Cabenuva section 1 (p.1) require suppression with no history of failure. Materiality is not shown. The candidate admits the addressable pool is unknown, and the per-1,000-patient figure (1,000 x 4,216.10 x 12 x 0.59 = $29.9M; arithmetic checks against the WAC rows 544-546) is about 0.1% of revenue. It applies the company-wide 41% GTN to a viremic, treatment-experienced population likely skewed to Medicaid/ADAP with deeper discounts. It also counts patients who were likely already on Biktarvy off-label, so the incremental revenue is unestablished. The epidemiology row (indication_epidemiology.csv) gives 65% suppression among diagnosed people, which mixes untreated and treated people, as the candidate concedes.
verdicts.correction: Keep as a qualitative label edge in the product section. Do not size it as revenue upside without a sourced count of resistance-free viremic treatment-experienced patients.

verdicts.argument: Biktarvy 14,334/29,443 = 48.7% checks (10-K index p.40; force_summary.csv GILD). The peer numbers have errors. ABBV is 22.5% in force_summary.csv, not 16.9%. The same table shows MRK Keytruda with expected selection in 2027 and expected_share_pct 48.7%, so on a forward basis Gilead is NOT uniquely the most concentrated single-drug name. NVO's 79.9% is a semaglutide franchise plus insulin, not one drug. 'Least tariff exposure' is not a differentiator: tariff_exempt_until is 2029-01-20 for every listed company, and GILD's non-U.S. site share (33.3%) ties BMY. The repatriation clause (10-K index p.21) is real, and a search of FY2025 peer 10-Ks found no equivalent disclosure. But it is conditional ('if the U.S. government is successful in increasing drug prices abroad'), it returns a portion of an INCREASE, so it cannot reduce current revenue, and it is unquantified. Nothing in the impact math touches revenue, OI or EPS.
verdicts.correction: Narrow to: Biktarvy is 48.7% of revenue, the highest share for any single drug already selected for IRA negotiation among the ten (MRK's Keytruda is expected to match it from 2029). Gilead is the only shortlist company whose 10-K discloses a term returning part of any future ex-U.S. price gains. That term is unquantified and conditional.

verdicts.argument: Biktarvy is the right product under a materiality lens: $14,334M, 48.7% of FY2025 revenue (10-K index p.40), with the IRA selection in 2028. The fine-print edge (label v22 p.1 vs Dovato and Cabenuva section 1) is verified. Its dollar effect is unquantified, though (see c08), so the product pick is material while the specific fine-print edge is not yet shown to be.
verdicts.correction: Keep Biktarvy. Frame the label edge as share defense in a niche, not as sized upside.

overall: Gilead's audited numbers are transcribed accurately throughout, and c05 (the $400M IP true-up kept in non-GAAP, recurring at $156M) and the narrowed c03 and c04 survive on materiality. The rest fail because the dollar impacts are invented scenarios (c01, c02, c06, c08), are mixed across years or between gross and net (c01, c03), are misattributed (c07), or rest on peer comparisons with wrong numbers (c09).
